# Automation and API

Dimension covering Notion's API, built-in automations, and integration ecosystem
compared to Obsidian's plugin model. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for
full source details.

## Notion API

### Rate Limits

"The rate limit for incoming requests per integration is an average of three
requests per second" [8]. Some bursts beyond the average are permitted but
specific burst parameters are not detailed [8].

Rate-limited requests return HTTP 429 with `rate_limited` error code and a
`Retry-After` header in seconds [8]. No tier-based differences currently; Notion
"may introduce distinct limits for different pricing plans in the future" [8].

### API Version 2025-09-03

Major update introducing "first-class support for multi-source databases" — a
single database with multiple linked data sources [18].

**Breaking changes** (not backwards-compatible) [18]:
- Page creation with database parents fails when additional data sources exist
- Database read/write/query operations fail
- Relation property updates targeting affected databases fail

**Restructuring** [18]:
- Database ID → Data Source ID transition
- New `/v1/data_sources` namespace replaces `/v1/databases`
- Retrieve Database endpoint returns list of child `data_sources`
- New Retrieve Data Source API for individual schemas

**New webhook events:** `data_source.content_updated`, `schema_updated`,
`created`, `moved`, `deleted`, `undeleted` [18].

**Migration:** 6-step process including TypeScript SDK upgrade to v5.0.0+ [18].

## Built-in Automations

Four automation types [19]:

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Buttons | General-purpose action triggers |
| Database Buttons | Automation within database entries |
| Database Automations | Trigger-action workflows on database events |
| Webhook Actions | External service integrations |

### Database Automations [19]

**Triggers:**
- New page added to database
- Specific property edited
- Any property edited (OR statements)

**Actions:**
- Update or complete properties
- Add/edit pages in same or different database
- Send Slack notifications
- Send Gmail notifications
- Trigger formula-based workflows

Plan restriction: "Database automations are only available on some plan types"
— specific tiers not documented in the source [19]. Advanced automations
(conditional logic in forms) require Business+ [3].

## Integration Ecosystem

Notion offers AI connectors for GitHub, Slack, Jira, Google Drive and other
services [1]. The API enables both internal and public integrations [18].

Import integrations include direct connections to Evernote, Trello, Google Docs,
Quip, Dropbox Paper, Hackpad, WorkFlowy, plus dedicated guides for Confluence,
Asana, and Monday.com [11].

## Obsidian Extensibility

Obsidian uses a community plugin architecture [17]:

- **Plugin count:** Thousands of community plugins (exact count not verified
  from official Obsidian plugin directory)
- **Plugin capabilities:** Kanban boards, calendar views, AI integrations,
  Dataview queries, Templater automation, REST API (community plugin)
- **API:** Open plugin API for local extensions
- **Integration model:** Plugins run locally within the app, not cloud-based

For detailed Obsidian plugin architecture, see
[obsidian-pa-integration](../../obsidian-pa-integration/).

## Comparison

| Capability | Notion | Obsidian |
|------------|--------|----------|
| API | REST API, 3 req/s per integration [8] | Community REST API plugin (local) |
| Automation | 4 built-in types [19] | Templater + community plugins |
| Webhooks | Native webhook events [18] | None (local-only) |
| Integration style | Cloud-based, vendor-managed | Local plugins, community-maintained |
| Extensibility model | API + marketplace | Open plugin API + community |

- Specific plan tiers for database automations are not documented in sources
- Obsidian plugin count (2,600+) comes from a single discovery-phase source
